subject.title: improve(i18n): generate native locales after merge

question: Should generated Android entries remain in the shared English `values/strings.xml` file, and if so what explicit source-versus-generated publication rule should permit both source PRs and the post-merge publisher without a mixed-artifact bypass?
rationale: The failing rule exposes a co-owned file boundary. Choosing whether to split the generated output, alter publication behavior, or define a narrowly scoped exception is an ownership and workflow-policy decision rather than a safe reviewer assumption.

options.title: Split generated and source ownership
options.body: Move generator-managed Android output to an independently publishable artifact path so source PRs and generated PRs have disjoint file ownership.

options.title: Retain the shared file with a narrow rule
options.body: Keep the current file layout but explicitly distinguish source-authorized and publisher-authorized changes, with tests proving neither path can bypass unrelated mixed diffs.

options.title: Pause the workflow change
options.body: Keep the current synchronous generated-artifact process until the base-resource ownership model is agreed.

recommendation.title: Split generated and source ownership
recommendation.body: Move generator-managed Android output to an independently publishable artifact path so source PRs and generated PRs have disjoint file ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied both the linked design proposal and the current implementation, making them the best available routing candidate for the intended ownership model.
